parts.gloss: has / is of the nature of

literal: As often as losing, desires, gambling-indeed like, suffering as often as, has love, the soul.
translation: Just as a gambler loves play all the more as he loses, so does the soul love life all the more as it suffers pain.
modern: சூதாட்டத்தில் இழக்க இழக்க மேலும் அதன் மேல் ஆசை கொள்ளும் சூதனைப் போல, துன்பங்களை அனுபவிக்க அனுபவிக்க இவ்வுயிர் உடலின் மேல் மேலும் பற்று வைக்கிறது.
explanation: This couplet uses a striking analogy to describe the persistent nature of attachment. The word 'இழத்தொறூஉம்' (as often as one loses) is paired with 'உழத்தொறூஉம்' (as often as one suffers) to show parallel behaviors. Just as a gambler cannot walk away and desires the game even more with every loss, the soul ('உயிர்') develops an even stronger attachment ('காதற்று') to worldly life the more it undergoes suffering ('துன்பம்'). The poet highlights the irrationality of human attachment through the self-destructive obsession of gambling.
